nodes.name: a-CoFeO-PO4
aliases: a-{ - } C o F e O { - } P O _ { 4 }

properties.description: Amorphous cobalt-iron oxide phosphate after oxygen evolution reaction

nodes.name: In-situ co-precipitation with phytic acid
nodes.procedure: 200 mg K₃[Fe(CN)₆] was dissolved in 40 mL deionized water and followed with pouring 4 mL phytic acid into the solution. After 20 min, 0.05 mol L⁻¹ Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O was added into the above mixture under fast stirring for 150 min. After the reaction completely finished, the PO₄³⁻ assistant precipitations were formed. Then, the synthesized precipitations were dried at 65 °C overnight and further heated at 400 °C (heating rate of 5 °C min⁻¹) for 2 h. The PO₄³⁻ assistant amorphous CoFeO was obtained after heating process.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows CoFeO consists of irregular stacked nanoparticles while a-CoFeO-PO₄ exhibits pore structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1a and Fig. S1, the CoFeO counterpart consists of irregular stacked nanoparticles. For the phytic acid introduced sample, some pore structures are emerged in as-formed materials (Fig. 1b and Fig. S2).

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing nanostructure with 50 nm scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of a-CoFeO-PO₄ is 48.09 m²/g and CoFeO is 12.65 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Brunauer Emmett Teller (BET) analysis were further recorded to explore the surface area and pore structure of samples. As exhibited in Fig. S3, the BET surface area of CoFeO counterpart is measured to be 12.65 m² g⁻¹, while that of the a-CoFeO-PO₄ increase to 48.09 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of a-CoFeO-PO₄ shows no observable lattice fringes confirming amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) image in Fig. 1c presents that no lattice fringes can be observed on a-CoFeO-PO₄.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image with lattice fringes and indexed planes

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms amorphous nature of a-CoFeO-PO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous nature is also confirmed by selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED) in Fig. 1d.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Co, Fe, O, and P in a-CoFeO-PO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectra (EDS) elemental mapping reveals presence of Co, Fe, O and P with uniform distribution in the a-CoFeO-PO₄ sample (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows Fe/Co ratio of 0.64 and P/Co ratio of 0.63 in a-CoFeO-PO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on ICP measurement, the ratio of Fe/Co is 0.64 and the ratio of P/Co is 0.63 (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows no significant diffraction peaks for amorphous a-CoFeO-PO₄; CoFeO shows peaks corresponding to CoFe bimetallic oxides (PDF#22-1086).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of as-prepared a-CoFeO-PO₄ and CoFeO counterpart were further proved by X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns. ... Whereas, no significant diffraction peaks can be detected in a-CoFeO-PO₄, indicating the amorphous state of metal oxides prepared by phytic acid assisted method (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Co 2p shows dominant Co²⁺ peaks at 782.3 eV and 798.1 eV in a-CoFeO-PO₄; Co²⁺/Co³⁺ coexist in CoFeO. Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ coexistence in both. P 2p peak at 133.4 eV confirms phosphate in a-CoFeO-PO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The core level of Co 2p in Fig. 2b presents the dominant peaks at 782.3 eV and 798.1 eV in a-CoFeO-PO₄ are characteristic peaks of Co²⁺. ... The high-resolution XPS spectrum for P 2p displays a peak at 133.4 eV (Fig. 2d), suggesting the P species in a-CoFeO-PO₄ is in form of oxidized phosphorus in phosphate (PO₄³⁻).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows a-CoFeO-PO₄ forms CoOOH (broad peak 500-600 cm⁻¹) at 1.4 V; CoFeO shows no CoOOH formation even at 1.5 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The initial peaks completely disappear and a board peak at 500-600 cm⁻¹ including various oxidation states of Co species in CoOOH emerges at 1.4 V (Fig. 3e). ... However, no signal of CoOOH species is detected even the potential reach to 1.5 V (Fig. 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-faradaic region gives Cdl of 0.54 mF/cm² (ECSA 2.64 cm²) for a-CoFeO-PO₄ before OER, increasing to 0.66 mF/cm² (ECSA 3.23 cm²) post-OER; CoFeO Cdl is 0.55 mF/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl for a-CoFeO-PO₄ and post-OER a-CoFeO-PO₄ is 0.54 mF cm⁻² and 0.66 mF cm⁻², respectively (Fig. S11). The ECSA values is 2.64 cm⁻² for a-CoFeO-PO₄ before OER process and that for post-OER a-CoFeO-PO₄ increases to 3.23 cm⁻². ... Moreover, the Cdl and ECSA for CoFeO are 0.55 mF cm⁻² and 2.69 cm⁻² (Fig. S12).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR confirms presence of phosphate species in a-CoFeO-PO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The P specie is further detected by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) measurement to confirm the type of phosphate (Fig. S6).
